rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance annual allowable rent increase (1.6% for 3/1/2026 - 2/28/2027)
rules.requirement: For rent-controlled units, landlords may raise rent each year by no more than the annual allowable increase published by the Rent Board. For March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 the allowable increase is 1.6% of base rent. To compute it, multiply base rent by .016; for example, $2,000.00 x .016 = $32.00, giving a new base rent of $2,032.00. Earlier periods were 1.4% (3/1/2025 - 2/28/2026) and 1.7% (3/1/2024 - 2/28/2025). The rate is reset each March 1. Units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, and tenancies eligible for a rent increase under Costa-Hawkins, are exempt from these limits but remain subject to just-cause eviction.
rules.key_value: 1.6% annual allowable increase for 3/1/2026-2/28/2027 (base rent x .016); prior 1.4% (2025-26), 1.7% (2024-25)

coverage.summary: Covers rent-controlled units under the San Francisco Rent Ordinance. Units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979 are exempt from the increase limits, as are Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies and some tenancies regulated by another agency. Covered units are exempt from the state cap (Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.12(d)(3)) because the local limit is stricter. Exempt San Francisco units may still fall under the state cap unless the state's own exemptions apply.

coverage.summary: Applies to rental units covered by the Rent Ordinance. This includes units exempt from the rent increase limits: units that first obtained a Certificate of Occupancy after June 13, 1979, Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies and some government-regulated tenancies. The just-cause provisions therefore cover units on both sides of the rent-limit cutoff. Where it applies, the state just-cause law (Cal. Civ. rules.title: San Francisco relocation payments for Ellis Act evictions (§ 37.9A)
rules.requirement: Tenants evicted under the Ellis Act must receive relocation payments. The amount is set per tenant and capped per unit. An additional amount is due for each elderly (62+) or disabled tenant. Amounts adjust each March 1 and depend on the date the notice of termination is served.

coverage.summary: Applies to tenants evicted when a landlord withdraws all rental units from the market under the state Ellis Act. The amount is fixed by the date the notice is served.

rules.title: San Francisco security deposit interest rate (4.2% for 3/1/2026 - 2/28/2027)
rules.requirement: Landlords holding tenant security deposits must pay interest at the annual rate published by the Rent Board. For March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 the rate is 4.2%. Prior rates were 5.0% (2025-26) and 5.2% (2024-25).

coverage.summary: The page gives only the annual interest rate and does not state which units are covered. The state deposit cap and return rules (Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5) apply alongside this local interest requirement.

rules.effective_date_note: The rate applies to March 1, 2026 - February 28, 2027 and is reset annually. The end of the period is not a sunset of the law.

rules.title: San Francisco ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices (Rent Ordinance § 37.10C)
rules.requirement: The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco. An algorithmic device is a device, such as a software program, that uses algorithms to analyze nonpublic competitor rental data to recommend to a landlord what rent to charge for a vacant unit. A tenant or the City Attorney may bring a civil action. Per a secondary source, tenants may seek damages, injunctive relief and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, and each month of use for each affected unit may be a separate violation.
rules.key_value: Ban on sale or use of algorithmic rent-setting devices; civil action by tenant or City Attorney; up to $1,000 per violation, each unit-month potentially separate (per secondary source); effective Oct. 14, 2024

coverage.summary: Applies to residential units in San Francisco and to sellers and users of qualifying algorithmic devices. No building exemptions are stated. It operates alongside the state Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms (Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729), which preserves other antitrust law.

rules.effective_date_note: The official Rent Board notice gives October 14, 2024. The Morgan Lewis alert's 'effective October 2024' is consistent.
rules.quoted_span: adding Section 37.10C to the Rent Ordinance went into effect on October 14, 2024. The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.
rules.review_note: The penalty amount and unit-month rule come only from a secondary law-firm alert (DX06); the ordinance text is not captured. The ordinance is at issue in Gomez v. Greystar Management Services LLC (N.D. Cal.). Enactment date not stated.
rules.source_notes: Official Rent Board news item (D081) is primary. Morgan Lewis alert dated Aug. 21, 2026 (DX06) is secondary.

also_supported_by.quoted_span: Each month of use for each affected dwelling unit may constitute a separate violation, and tenants may seek damages, injunctive relief, and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation.
